root_cause.text: The `list->last_gc` timestamp was updated on every new connection insertion rather than only when garbage collection (GC) was actually performed, allowing high packet rates to continuously reset the GC timer and indefinitely postpone cleanup, causing the connection count list to grow without bound.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the `list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;` from inside the new-node addition path (line 252 removed) to after the connection lookup and potential GC path (line 232 added). The CVE description states: "last_gc is being updated everytime a new connection is tracked... With a sufficiently high packet rate, it is possible to always bypass the GC, causing the list to grow infinitely."

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds 'list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;' at the end of __nf_conncount_add after adding a new node, and also updates it after GC in nf_conncount_gc_list. This means the last_gc timestamp is updated on every connection insertion, not only when GC is performed. Consequently, the early-return checks in both __nf_conncount_add ('if (time_is_after_eq_jiffies((unsigned long)list->last_gc))') and nf_conncount_gc_list will always see a recent timestamp, preventing garbage collection from ever running. This exactly matches the root cause: updating last_gc on insertion allows high packet rates to indefinitely postpone cleanup.
